passage:
On the village school ground, a white sheet hung between two poles for the open-air film. When the dark forest music began, Reena pulled her dupatta over her eyes.
A hand found hers. It was Yusuf's, sticky from peanuts. He said nothing, only squeezed.
Her breath came easier and she peeked through her fingers. "It's only a film," he whispered, not letting go.
Later, when a loud clap of thunder sounded in the story, Yusuf flinched. This time Reena held his hand tight.

qa.q: What did Yusuf's hand feel like?
How did Reena feel when Yusuf held her hand?
qa.a: She felt less alone and calmer: her breathing eased and she dared to peek through her fingers. 🙂

qa.q: What might Reena take from this moment?
qa.a: She may learn that a quiet hand can comfort a scared friend, which she then does for Yusuf at the thunder scene.

qa.q: Why might Yusuf have taken Reena's hand without speaking?
qa.a: He may have noticed she was scared and wanted her to feel supported, and his own flinch later suggests he knows how scary it can be.

grounding: A friend holds the child's hand during the scary part of the film, and she feels less alone and later does the same.

passage: The colony was showing a film on a sheet between two trees, but halfway through, the power cut out. The generator coughed and the picture came back, darker and louder, just as the wolf jumped out. Yogesh squeezed his eyes shut. He wanted to run home but it was dark all around. Then a small hand slid into his. It was Ganga, sitting next to him on the mat. "I'll hold on till the wolf goes," she whispered. Yogesh held tight. He peeked. The wolf ran away. He let out a long breath and didn't let go until the end.

qa.q: Where was the film being shown?
qa.a: It was shown on a sheet between two trees in the colony.

qa.q: How did Yogesh feel when Ganga took his hand?
qa.a: He felt less alone and less scared, so he held on tight and could peek again.

qa.q: What could Yogesh do for someone else one day?
qa.a: He could hold a scared friend's hand, just as Ganga did for him.

qa.q: Why might Ganga have taken Yogesh's hand?
qa.a: Ganga probably saw Yogesh was frightened and felt for him, maybe feeling a little scared too.

grounding: A young boy is scared during a film, and his friend holds his hand so he feels less alone.

passage: At Chaitanya's birthday party in the Bengaluru flat, the children sat on the carpet watching a cartoon. When the big storm came in the film and the little boat started to sink, Ramesh pulled his knees up and covered his ears. Chaitanya, the birthday boy, noticed. He shuffled over and held Ramesh's hand. "The boat's okay. I've seen it. Hold on." Ramesh held on. The boat bobbed back up. Ramesh laughed shakily. Later, when a younger cousin cried at the thunder in the film, Ramesh went and sat beside him. "Hold my hand. It gets better."

qa.q: How did Ramesh feel when Chaitanya held his hand?
qa.a: He felt less alone and calmer, able to watch the scary part.

qa.q: What did Ramesh do later that shows what he learned?
qa.a: He held a younger cousin's hand during the scary thunder, doing what Chaitanya had done for him.

qa.q: How might Chaitanya feel seeing Ramesh comfort the cousin?
qa.a: He may feel happy and proud that his kindness was passed on.

grounding: A young boy is scared during a film and his friend holds his hand, and later he does the same for a younger child.
